chains.title: No TF-mediated allelic effect at this exact base; signal reflects linked causal variant or locus context
predictions: No reproducible allele-specific TF binding distinguishes ref C from alt A at this exact base.
The LMO1 association is driven by a linked causal variant or broader LMO1 locus context rather than this nucleotide.
The many ChIP peaks at the element reflect general active-element occupancy, not an allele-specific effect of C>A.
falsified_if: A robust allele-specific binding assay shows a clear ref/alt difference for a TF at this base.
CRISPR editing this exact nucleotide changes LMO1 enhancer activity or LMO1 expression in SK-N-SH.
Fine-mapping shows this base, rather than a linked variant, is causal.

chains.title: GATA3 binds the ref C allele at the LMO1 enhancer and sustains LMO1 expression

links.claim: GATA3 is ChIP-bound at this element in SK-N-SH and expressed there (E06, E04). Locus literature shows that a protective low-LMO1 allele at the LMO1 super-enhancer ablates GATA3 binding (E19b), and the provided eQTL reports alt A with lower LMO1 (E17). I therefore infer that ref C preserves GATA3 binding more than alt A, but the published GATA3-ablating SNP is not this exact C>A and no QBiC-SELEX model or allele-specific assay for this base is given, so the direction is locus-level inference.
The variant sits in EH38E1518342, an active distal enhancer-like cCRE, and the locus is described as an LMO1 super-enhancer.

LMO1 is the proximal gene and strongest L2G target. GTEx skeletal muscle shows alt A with lower LMO1 (NES -0.13), while Brain_Cortex has no significant eQTL in the provided data; this supports LMO1 as target but does not establish neuroblastoma-cell direction.
GATA3 occupancy at this element is reported in the matched SK-N-SH neuroblastoma biosample.

LMO1 is a neuroblastoma predisposition/oncogene candidate and LMO1-expressing neuroblastoma cells show pro-metastatic behavior. The provided GWAS credible sets are not neuroblastoma, so the exact-variant disease link remains indirect.

predictions: Allele-specific GATA3 ChIP, EMSA or MPRA in SK-N-SH shows ref C > alt A at the exact C>A base.
CRISPR editing C>A at the endogenous locus lowers LMO1 enhancer activity or LMO1 expression in SK-N-SH.
GATA3 knockdown reduces LMO1 expression/enhancer activity more than GATA2 knockdown.
falsified_if: Alt A binds GATA3 more strongly than ref C, or GATA3 binding is not allele-specific at this base.
GATA3 depletion does not reduce LMO1 expression or enhancer activity in SK-N-SH.
The C>A edit increases rather than decreases LMO1 expression in the neuroblastoma context.

chains.title: GATA2, rather than GATA3, binds the ref C allele and activates LMO1

links.claim: GATA2 is ChIP-bound at this element in SK-N-SH and is highly expressed there (E05, E04). GATA2 has no QBiC-SELEX model in the provided evidence, and there is no allele-specific GATA2 binding measurement. I infer that ref C binds GATA2 more strongly because the locus implicates a GATA motif, but this is a GATA-family inference, not direct GATA2 evidence.
The variant lies in EH38E1518342, a distal enhancer-like cCRE with DNase and H3K27ac signal, and multiple active-element factor ChIP peaks in SK-N-SH.

The element is in the LMO1 gene body and LMO1 is the strongest L2G target. GTEx reports an LMO1 eQTL in skeletal muscle with alt A NES -0.13, but there is no Brain_Cortex eQTL in the provided data; the direction in neuroblastoma is not established.
GATA2 occupancy at this element is reported in the matched SK-N-SH neuroblastoma biosample.

LMO1 is a neuroblastoma-associated gene and LMO1-expressing neuroblastoma cells show pro-migratory/pro-invasive behavior. However, the exact variant lacks a provided neuroblastoma GWAS signal, so the phenotype link is indirect.

predictions: Allele-specific GATA2 ChIP or EMSA in SK-N-SH shows ref C > alt A at this base.
GATA2 knockdown reduces LMO1 enhancer activity or LMO1 expression in SK-N-SH, while GATA3 knockdown does not.
The alt A allele lowers LMO1 expression when GATA2 is present.
falsified_if: GATA2 binding is not allele-specific or alt A binds GATA2 more than ref C.
GATA2 depletion does not change LMO1 expression or enhancer activity in SK-N-SH.
GATA3, not GATA2, accounts for the allele-specific GATA-factor binding at this base.

grades_v0.reason: GATA2 ChIP-seq occupancy at the variant in SK-N-SH is shown (E05, E04), but there is no QBiC-SELEX or allele-specific binding measurement; the claimed alt>A direction is inferred only. Occupancy without an allele-specific change is weak support for the binding link.
E03 directly places the variant in EH38E1518342, a dELS with DNase and H3K27ac signal, and E04 reports multiple active-element factor ChIP peaks in SK-N-SH.

E02 and E16 support LMO1 as the proximal/L2G target, but the cited eQTL E17 is in skeletal muscle, not SK-N-SH, and NES -0.13 for alt A indicates lower LMO1 expression, opposite to the activation direction claimed in H1.
E05 reports GATA2 ChIP-seq peaks containing the variant in the matching SK-N-SH biosample, with E04 confirming the matched active-element context.

E18a supports a role for LMO1-expressing neuroblastoma cells in migration/matrix degradation, but this is not germline risk evidence and does not show that this variant alters LMO1 expression. E15/E16 provide no neuroblastoma association for this variant.
GATA3 ChIP-seq occupancy at the variant in SK-N-SH is shown (E06), but no QBiC-SELEX or allele-specific binding data support the inferred alt>A direction. This is only occupancy evidence.
E03 places the variant in an active dELS, and E04 shows GATA3 among the factors ChIP-bound in SK-N-SH at this element, consistent with a GATA-factor-bound enhancer.
LMO1 is supported as the target gene by proximity and L2G (E02, E16), but the GTEx eQTL (E17) is skeletal muscle and its alt-A NES is negative, contradicting the activation direction claimed for H2.
E06 reports GATA3 ChIP-seq peaks containing the variant in the matching SK-N-SH neuroblastoma biosample.

The neuroblastoma phenotype link relies on LMO1 biology from E18/E18a, not on evidence that this variant or GATA3 binding changes LMO1 expression in neuroblastoma; E15/E16 lack a neuroblastoma association for this variant.
YY1 ChIP-seq occupancy at the variant in SK-N-SH is shown (E10), but the claimed ref>C binding direction and loss of a YY1 motif are inferred, with no QBiC-SELEX or allele-specific binding data.
E03 supports that the variant lies in an active dELS, but the additional claim that YY1 acts as a repressor at such elements is not supported by the cited evidence.

LMO1 is supported as the proximal/L2G target, but E17 reports alt-A lower LMO1 expression in skeletal muscle, which conflicts with the H3 prediction that loss of ref-bound YY1 repression on alt A would increase LMO1.
E10 reports YY1 ChIP-seq peaks containing the variant in the matching SK-N-SH biosample.

The phenotype link is indirect: LMO1 is implicated in neuroblastoma biology (E18/E18a), but there is no evidence that YY1 binding at this base changes LMO1 expression or neuroblastoma risk, and no neuroblastoma GWAS association is provided.

grades_final.reason: GATA2 ChIP occupancy at the element in SK-N-SH is shown (E05/E04), but the claim's ref>C allele-specific direction is inferred from GATA-family/locus context, not measured at this base; no QBiC-SELEX or allele-specific assay is provided. Occupancy alone makes this weak.
E03 directly places the variant in EH38E1518342, a dELS with DNase/H3K27ac signal, and E04 reports multiple active-element factor ChIP peaks containing the variant in the matched SK-N-SH biosample.

LMO1 is the proximal gene in the gene body and the strongest L2G target (E02/E16), and E17 reports an LMO1 eQTL, but that eQTL is in skeletal muscle rather than neuroblastoma and the direction in SK-N-SH is not established. Gene link is indirect.
E05 and E04 report GATA2 ChIP-seq peaks containing the variant in SK-N-SH, the matched neuroblastoma biosample.

LMO1 is a neuroblastoma-associated gene and LMO1-expressing neuroblastoma cells show pro-migratory behavior (E18a/E21), but no neuroblastoma GWAS or credible set for this exact variant is provided. The phenotype link is locus-level indirect.

GATA3 ChIP occupancy at the element in SK-N-SH is shown (E06/E04), but allele-specific ref>C binding at this exact C>A is inferred from a different SNP (E19b G>T) and from eQTL direction; no QBiC-SELEX or allele-specific assay at this base is provided. This is indirect.
E03 directly places the variant in EH38E1518342, an active dELS, and E04 shows factor ChIP peaks containing the variant in SK-N-SH; E19a supports that the LMO1 locus contains a super-enhancer.
LMO1 is proximal and the strongest L2G target, and E17 shows an LMO1 eQTL, but the eQTL is in skeletal muscle not neuroblastoma; direction in SK-N-SH is not established. Gene link is indirect.
E06 and E04 report GATA3 ChIP-seq peaks containing the variant in SK-N-SH, the matched neuroblastoma biosample.
LMO1 is a neuroblastoma predisposition/oncogene candidate (E18a/E21), but the provided GWAS credible sets for this exact variant are not neuroblastoma. The disease link remains indirect.

checks.args_json: {"query":"LMO1 neuroblastoma enhancer GATA2 GATA3 allele-specific binding"}
checks.why: A literature search could find allele-specific ChIP, EMSA, reporter, or MPRA evidence at the LMO1 enhancer that would directly test whether alt A binds GATA2/GATA3 more than ref C.
Testing LMO1 eQTL direction in a neural GTEx tissue would help determine whether alt A is associated with higher or lower LMO1 expression, addressing the direction conflict with E17.

Open Targets evidence for LMO1-neuroblastoma association would clarify whether the phenotype link is supported beyond general LMO1 neuroblastoma literature, though it still would not prove this variant is causal.
